action: As NCCIA's Director General urges, victims of blackmail or harassment should come forward and approach NCCIA immediately for assistance.
date_note: APP's dateline is 24 November and the spokesperson spoke on Tuesday; the page gives no earlier day for the arrest.
exec: Shows Pakistan's cybercrime agency acting on online blackmail of women; no business action implied.
geo_basis: agency location (NCCIA, Islamabad, as stated in the article)
plain: Pakistan's cybercrime agency says it arrested a man accused of posing as a British citizen, promising marriage, secretly recording women and blackmailing them for money.
summary: Pakistan's NCCIA arrested Irfan Siddique, an NCCIA spokesperson said, according to APP. The agency alleges he lured women with fake job advertisements, posed as a British citizen with a fake identity card, promised marriage, secretly recorded private videos and used them to extort money. Investigators are still working to identify additional victims.
title: Pakistan's NCCIA arrests suspect accused of blackmailing women under a fake British identity

validation.note: Single publisher (APP) relaying an NCCIA spokesperson's statement; no second publisher read.
